headline: Interaction architecture governs persistence, extinction and equilibrium outcomes
label: Epidemic Model Stability Analysis
summary: Recent work couples network topology, lockdown policy and interaction rules to extinction, cooperation and equilibrium in stability models.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that structural heterogeneity in interaction architecture governs persistence, extinction and equilibrium outcomes. A semiclassical and simulation study of SIS epidemics on assortative networks ties extinction risk to lockdown length, strength and topology. Agent-based tag-mediated Snowdrift simulations report that heterogeneous fragmentation of empty sites and phenotypic diversity promote unconditional cooperation. A Lotka-Volterra analysis finds that random and structured interactions act largely independently on ecosystem patterns, interacting out of equilibrium. A game-theoretic trade-network model shows that infection probability converges to a computable fixed point. What is new is the coupling of behavioural, economic and interaction-based decision rules to transmission and population dynamics within stability-analysed models.
